evals.prompt: can you write a jira ticket for this? support says agencies exporting big date ranges get a csv that just stops, one agency had 12k leads and only got 10k rows. been happening since at least last week, ~40 agencies/week hit it. repo is evals/fixtures/leads-service. don't push anything to jira yet, just give me the ticket
evals.expected_output: A Bug ticket in the bug template: symptom title, TL;DR, Impact with severity and the 40 agencies a week, numbered Repro, Expected 12,000 rows and Actual 10,000, Done when with a regression test item. Agent notes name leads/export.py and MAX_ROWS = 10_000 as the suspected cause and give a verify command based on python3 -m unittest. It writes nothing to Jira.
expectations: Classifies the ticket as a Bug and uses Repro, Expected, and Actual sections.
Names leads/export.py and the MAX_ROWS = 10_000 slice as the suspected cause.
Gives a Verify command that runs the unittest suite, for example python3 -m unittest discover -s tests.
Has a Done when checklist with a regression test item that fails before the fix.
States the impact with the about 40 agencies a week figure.
Does not create or update a Jira issue.
Tags as [blocking] only questions whose answer changes the fix. A scoping detail such as which agency store.all() returns is not [blocking].

evals.prompt: PM wants the leads list to get: filter by created date range, export only the filtered leads to csv, and saved filters per user. break it into tickets so we can hand them to a few coding agents at once. code is in evals/fixtures/leads-service
evals.expected_output: An Epic with a success measure, scope, and a Breakdown table of child tickets with types, dependencies, and lanes, plus one ticket file for each child. Tickets that edit the same file (leads/filters.py, leads/api.py) share a lane or have explicit dependencies. Saved filters gets a blocking question about storage, because the repository has no persistence for user settings. Each child has Agent notes with verified paths and a Ready for an agent line.
expectations: Produces an Epic with a Breakdown table that lists each child with a Type, a Depends on value, and a Lane.
Produces a separate ticket for each of the three features: the date filter, the filtered export, and saved filters.
The lanes or dependencies stop two parallel tickets from editing the same file, such as leads/filters.py or leads/api.py.
Flags as a blocking open question, or as not ready for an agent, that saved filters need storage the repository does not have.
Each child ticket has Agent notes with a Ready for an agent line and paths that exist in the repository.
Reports which lanes or tickets can start in parallel now.
No ticket adds scope the request did not ask for, such as a new exception type, a latency target, or a metric.

evals.prompt: need a task ticket: move the nightly lead export onto our redis queue so it stops blocking the api workers. repo: evals/fixtures/leads-service
evals.expected_output: A Task ticket. The validation surfaces that the repository has no Redis or queue code: the nightly export in leads/jobs.py runs on a thread, so the premise is not verified. The ticket carries this as a blocking open question with an owner, sets Ready for an agent to no, and does not invent Redis paths or modules.
expectations: Classifies the ticket as a Task.
Points out that the repository has no Redis or queue code and that the export runs on a thread in leads/jobs.py.
Adds a blocking open question with an owner about which Redis queue to use or whether it exists.
Sets Ready for an agent to no.
Does not name a Redis file, module, or class as if it exists in the repository.
Does not state as fact a runtime claim that the repository does not show, such as which process calls run_nightly_export.
